rejected_reasons.REQ-0025: off-target: Two unlicensed False paths: (1) release case: the check treats any sda_oen 0->1 with sda_i==0 as an activation and fails if al is not 1, but the sentence only requires al when that release+low-sda occurs "during arbitration checking". The check's TRIGGER would have to be narrowed to include the arbitration-checking condition (whatever observable port or condition the spec uses to indicate arbitration-checking / active arbitration) or otherwise only open when the surrounding text licences it. (2) STOP case: the check treats any SDA rising while SCL==1 and sda_oen==1 as an activation and fails if al is not 1, but the sentence requires this only when a bit-level command is active AND the STOP was not requested by this controller. The check must add the observable condition that a bit-level command is active (or use the route's activation condition) and must exclude STOPs that the controller itself requested. Deleting the offending assertions is not the intended fix — the correct repair is to tighten the activations (the check's TRIGGER) so they match the obligation's qualifications.
rejected_reasons.REQ-0037: off-target: The check never asserts the EFFECT the sentence requires. There are no False paths because the code returns UNKNOWN rather than convicting a design that lets cnt change or clk_en go high while slave_wait is true. To test the requirement the check must keep its trigger (open on scl_oen==1 and scl_i==0, close on scl_i==1 or scl_oen==0, abort on reset) but add an assertion over those windows that implements the effect at a declared port: e.g. throughout each activation window assert that clk-driven progress is suspended by observing that clk_en-driven outputs do not change (candidate observable ports mentioned in the spec: scl_o, sda_o, dout, cmd_ack, busy) or use a declared observed_via port that carries clk_en. As written the checker only locates activations and correctly reports unobservability, but it does not test the requirement's effect.
rejected_reasons.REQ-0038: not-assertable: effect: the requirement's asserted effect is 'slave_wait' (and it depends on filtered 'sSCL'), both of which are internal signals not exported on any declared port; there is no declared port named by this sentence that would show the required difference, so the obligation is not observable/decidable at the interface.
rejected_reasons.REQ-0040: not-assertable: Visibility is missing. The requirement forbids a behaviour of internal signals (slave_wait asserted and internal counter 'cnt' advancing) but does not say how this difference would appear on any declared port. The trigger references an internal signal (slave_wait) and the effect references an internal counter (cnt); neither is exposed in the interface or via observed_via. Because of that missing observable port the check must abstain. To make the requirement testable the text must state which declared output(s) show that cnt is paused (or expose slave_wait), or provide an observed_via route that maps the effect to a port.
rejected_reasons.REQ-0041: not-assertable: The requirement lacks visibility of its EFFECT: the sentence requires assertion of the internal signal 'scl_sync' but that signal is not a declared port in the interface, so no trace-level check can observe or convict a design for failing to assert it. To make this decidable a declared output (or probe) that reflects scl_sync must be named (or the requirement must rephrase the effect at a declared port). Because the obligation is unobservable, the rest of the check's licensing (False paths) does not apply.
rejected_reasons.REQ-0042: not-assertable: effect: the sentence lacks a DUT obligation. It describes/labels an observation (that a fall while released indicates another master forced SCL low) but does not state a required change or required value on any port that a check could convict. To make this testable the requirement would need an effect phrased as an obligation (e.g. "when scl_i falls while scl_oen==1, the controller SHALL record/raise <port> indicating arbitration lost" or similar).
rejected_reasons.REQ-0048: not-assertable: The requirement omits the observable effect / port: it names an internal sta_condition but does not say where START detection is reported at the module boundary. To make this testable the sentence must name an output (or otherwise declare how detection is observable) so a check can assert its value. (No False path to repair in the code; the missing piece is the effect visibility/port in the requirement.)
rejected_reasons.REQ-0049: not-assertable: effect (observable consequence). The sentence defines the internal predicate sto_condition but does not state what external port or observable behaviour must indicate a STOP; there is no trigger+observable effect pair for a check to decide. (Because of that, no False path in the code is licensed.)
rejected_reasons.REQ-0051: off-target: The check produces False verdicts that are not licensed by the sentence. Specifically: (1) it convicts a design that drives al high on the cycle immediately after the arbitration-lost observation because it requires al==1 on the activation row; to fix, the assertion should allow al to appear on the activation row OR immediately after (e.g. use an eventually/pulse centered on the activation). (2) it convicts designs that assert al transiently (pulse then deassert) while the activation continues because the check requires al==1 throughout the entire window to TO_END; to fix, the windowed assertion should require al to be observed (become 1) at or shortly after the observation, not remain 1 for the whole activation. (Additionally, the use of after(...) opens windows only on rising activations and may miss cases where the activation holds from trace start; that yields None rather than a False, not a wrongful conviction, but should be considered when repairing.)
rejected_reasons.REQ-0052: off-target: The check's trigger is too broad: it opens on sda rise while scl_i==1 and ena==1 but does not require that the CURRENT COMMAND is not a STOP. That omission lets the check return False (al==0) in cases the requirement explicitly excludes (when the current command IS a STOP). To fix, the opening predicate must be narrowed to include the requirement's full trigger — i.e. the STOP-shaped event occurring while the FSM is active AND the current command is not STOP (this must be established by the observable activation route or by the appropriate prior-activation window). Do not invent a numeric encoding for STOP in this repair; instead use the spec's activation/context or an observable route that establishes “current command != STOP.”
rejected_reasons.REQ-0055: not-assertable: effect: the obligation sentence does not state the concrete, testable relation (that dout equals the sampled/filtered SDA at each rising edge of SCL during a READ). The supporting span supplies the sampling instant and the equality, but the obligation itself names only a capability; no port-level effect is asserted in the obligation to be tested. The check correctly abstains rather than asserting the supporting-span claim.
rejected_reasons.REQ-0059: off-target: The check's TRIGGER is wrong. It opens windows on any cmd_ack rising edge rather than on the requirement's trigger, the end of a command sequence. Because of that the check can return False (1) when a cmd_ack rise occurs outside an end-of-sequence, or (2) when busy is not deasserted at a rise that is unrelated to the completion event — situations the requirement does not condemn. To fix: open the window on the end-of-command-sequence activation (the normalized activation/route condition) or otherwise filter cmd_ack rises so only those that coincide with the end-of-sequence are used as the opener. Keep the pulse and busy assertions inside that correctly-scoped window. (Note: the check also currently returns None when no cmd_ack rise is observed; if the author wants a conviction for a missing pulse at an end-of-sequence, the window must be opened on the end-of-sequence event rather than on the cmd_ack rise.)
rejected_reasons.REQ-0061: off-target: The unlicensed False path is the check's assumption that the activation-row outputs define the 'released' level and that a later row must equal those activation values (released_both). The obligation requires a release then the specific pull sequence, but it does not say that the activation row encodes the released level nor that the released state must appear on a row after activation. To fix: change the check's trigger so the window opens on the row that actually shows the release (e.g. open when cmd==1 AND sda_oen and scl_oen indicate released), or allow the sequence to accept the activation row as satisfying the initial 'released' step (do not exclude the activation row). In short, the check must not hard-code the activation-row values as the released level — either move the trigger to the observed release row or permit the activation row to satisfy the first sequence predicate.
rejected_reasons.REQ-0062: off-target: The check incorrectly fixes on the first two sda_oen transitions in the STOP window. To avoid unlicensed False verdicts the check must look for the existence of some SDA drive-then-release pair (not necessarily the first two transitions) that has a SCL release between the SDA drive and SDA release and with cmd_ack asserted after that SDA release. Concretely: replace the 'take the first two sda edges' logic with a search over all ordered SDA-edge pairs (i<j) inside the window and accept if any pair has an intervening SCL edge and a cmd_ack at or after the later SDA edge. The unlicensed False paths are the 'no SCL transition between the two SDA transitions' and the 'cmd_ack before e_sda2' outcomes when those checks were applied to a spurious early pair of SDA transitions rather than to the actual STOP-shaped SDA pair; the check's TRIGGER/window should remain cmd==2 && ena==1 until cmd_ack, but the assertion must be changed from 'first-two-edges' ordering to 'exists a pair of SDA transitions satisfying the ordering with SCL and cmd_ack'.
rejected_reasons.REQ-0063: off-target: The check is too specific about transitions: it requires explicit rising edges for sda_oen and for scl_oen within the read window. The requirement only requires that sda_oen be released (sda_oen == 1) during the read sample window and that scl_oen be 1 during the sample window and then become 0 afterwards. To fix: stop testing for rises (edges) and instead test the port values (e.g. eventually/throughout on outputs.sda_oen == 1 during the sample window; and require that there exists a later row with outputs.scl_oen == 0). Concretely, replace sda_release_pred and scl_released_pred (edge-based) with predicates that check outputs['sda_oen'] == 1 and outputs['scl_oen'] == 1 so the check does not convict designs where the lines are already released at window start.
rejected_reasons.REQ-0065: off-target: The check fails to treat activation aborts as voiding the completion window. The normalized activation lists aborts_on: al==1, nReset==0, rst==1; the code must pass these conditions to after(..., aborts=...) (or otherwise exclude activation rows where an abort is active) so that a busy fall occurring with an abort does not open a window that can be strongly failed. As written, the check will return False for a completion that is actually aborted (e.g. arbitration lost or reset at that instant), but the obligation says nothing that condemns failing to assert cmd_ack in aborted completions. Fix: exclude abort rows from the trigger (use after(..., aborts= [{"al":1},{"nReset":0},{"rst":1}]) or equivalent) so only non-aborted completions are checked.
rejected_reasons.REQ-0069: not-assertable: states_an_obligation: both trigger and effect are missing — the sentence names a documentation/header only and provides no activation condition or observable effect on any declared port. tests_the_requirement: n/a (the oracle properly abstains; there are no unlicensed False paths).
rejected_reasons.REQ-0072: not-assertable: The requirement's EFFECT is not visible on any declared port: it requires internal sampling into cSCL/cSDA but does not state any observable consequence on the interface. To make this decidable the requirement must state the effect on a declared port (for example expose the synchronizer outputs as probes, or state a visible consequence of sampling). As written there is no observable claim to test, so the check correctly returns UNKNOWN rather than producing a False; the missing piece is the observable effect (visibility).
rejected_reasons.REQ-0078: not-assertable: The obligation's EFFECT is not visible on any declared port: the sentence says the module shall "detect" a START (internal event) but names no output or observable behaviour that would show that detection. To make this decidable the requirement must name the port (or existing observable signal) that indicates START was detected (for example tie the detection to a declared output such as busy, cmd_ack, sda_oen, or add an observed_via route).
rejected_reasons.REQ-0079: not-assertable: effect (observable port): the obligation names the detection event but does not say what the module must do or where that detection is reported. To make this decidable the sentence must name the port or observable behaviour that indicates a STOP was detected (e.g. a named output or probe that is asserted/pulsed on STOP).
